# The four things only a run can show

## pnpm dev serves all three apps

`pnpm dev` against the running stack: `GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/health` answers
`{"status":"ok","service":"@seen/api","core":"@seen/core"}`, `http://127.0.0.1:3000/`
answers 200, and the worker compiles clean and holds its BullMQ connection to the
compose Redis.

Two things had to be fixed to get there, both real and both now committed. `import.meta.url`
in the boundary walker broke the CommonJS build of every app that imports the provider
package, so the repository root is found by walking up to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` instead;
it is the one lookup that works the same under tsc and under vitest. And `nest-cli.json`
resolves `entryFile` against `outDir`, which with this repository's root-level `rootDir`
means `apps/<app>/src/main`, not a path relative to the app.

## The Postmark fixture, replayed against the running server

    $ pnpm replay:inbound
    {"threadId":"3ec7dca3-b797-4ab8-b3e1-1b93fbd99e9f","created":true}
    $ pnpm replay:inbound apps/api/src/webhooks/fixtures/postmark-inbound-reply.json
    {"threadId":"3ec7dca3-b797-4ab8-b3e1-1b93fbd99e9f","created":false}

The reply joined the thread the first mail opened rather than starting a second one.

## The collector prints traces and per-tenant cost lines

From `docker compose logs otel-collector`, on spans the provider sent over OTLP/HTTP:

    -> seen.tenant_id: Str(demo-tenant)
    -> seen.operation: Str(agent.draft_claim)
    -> seen.model: Str(claude-opus-5)
    -> seen.cost_cents: Int(7)
    -> seen.currency: Str(EUR)

## The tunnel

`pnpm tunnel` took the local api to `https://infections-collapse-boss-cursor.trycloudflare.com`.
Over that URL, with TLS verifying: `/health` answered 200 with the api's own body, and
a POST of the inbound fixture to `/webhooks/postmark/inbound` answered 202 with the
thread id the local replay had already created. The tunnel was closed immediately
afterwards and the same URL then answered 530, which is what a closed quick tunnel
answers.

One environment note for whoever runs this next: `curl` inside this session could not
resolve the trycloudflare hostname although `dig` resolved it, so the checks above went
through `curl --resolve`. That is this shell's resolver, not the tunnel; a browser on
the same machine reaches the URL directly.
